rationale: Both candidates converge on the same core technical findings (untouched sibling BNSD call sites, ndim conflation bug, non-contiguous return, undertested B*N boundary, uncited magic numbers) but neither directly recalls the GT's central ask for a three-way perf comparison, only tangentially recovering the 'shared/model-independent helper' concern via the sibling-call-site angle. X is more disciplined about grounding: it hedges unverifiable claims explicitly ('treated as evidence, not CI-verified') and backs nearly every finding with quoted file:line evidence, whereas Y asserts specific unverifiable outcomes (an exact RuntimeError message from a claimed run, a flat 'CI is red on merged head' status) that read as overclaimed rather than diff-grounded. Both are equally concrete and actionable with file/line citations and proposed fixes.
